candidates.title: Elastic Gang: Per-Token Membership Change for a Hard-Barriered LLM Inference Gang Co-Scheduled with OS Processes
candidates.abstract: On-device LLM decoding is a hard-barriered CPU-SIMD computation that wants every core for milliseconds per token, while the rest of the OS wants those same cores continuously. A barriered gang cannot simply be dropped into a preemptive scheduler: an unannounced departure deadlocks a barrier, and an unannounced arrival silently corrupts logits. I present the elastic gang of Anima OS, a bare-metal x86-64 Rust kernel in which the inference gang is a first-class schedulable entity whose core membership may change between any two tokens. The core mechanism is an ACK-latched epoch protocol that never waits on a named core: a seqlock-style generation-tagged latch composed with RCU/epoch-style membership consent, so each token's participant set is the intersection of the cores the gang requested and the cores that acked the current epoch. An un-acked core is outside this token and joins at most one token later. Displaced general processes migrate and keep running; cores return to them the moment a generation ends. On a real AMD Zen 5 machine (8C/16T), inference output is bit-exact under verified per-token membership change on both a 135M and a 7B model, the property that makes elasticity safe in a kernel whose safety gate reads logits. Against fair static core partitions, elastic membership Pareto-dominates: at intermediate inference duty cycles it delivers 1.75x (25%), 1.52x (50%), and 1.28x (75%) the general throughput of a static 8-core split at equal or better inference throughput, recovers all eight stranded cores when inference is idle, and converges to the split at saturation. Returning a lent core costs 0.22 us (p50); acquiring a busy, tenant-occupied core costs one scheduling quantum (~16 ms): a running tenant is never preempted mid-slice. Decode throughput saturates at gang width 8, so ceding cores past the knee is nearly free: elasticity auto-sizes the gang online.
candidates.reason: オンデバイスLLMデコードのハードバリア型ギャングをOSプロセスと共スケジュールするため、トークン単位でコア所属を変更できるACKラッチ付きエポックプロトコルをベアメタルカーネルで実装しビット完全性を保つ研究であり、推論スケジューリングへの直接貢献として採用する。

candidates.title: Think Before You Speak: Enabling Training-Free Latent Communication Between Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in solving complex tasks in coding, mathematical logic, and iterative reasoning, especially by coordinating effectively within multi-agent systems (MAS). However, language agents traditionally communicate via text exchange, which introduces a bottleneck in information transfer and adds prefill latency for downstream agents. Recent work proposes that directly sharing the key-value (KV) cache between language models can enable efficient latent collaboration, entirely bypassing standard text-based communication. To enable latent communication between heterogeneous models of different sizes, prior work introduces trained fusion adapters for each model pair, which limits practical deployment. We introduce CacheFuse, a training-free method which demonstrates that augmenting a downstream model with an upstream model's KV cache using linear interpolation consistently enables superior performance than the standalone downstream model can achieve. We systematically analyze CacheFuse across four reasoning and knowledge benchmarks and demonstrate up to 8.6 percentage points higher accuracy compared to single-model baselines and up to 12.2x TTFT speedup compared to text-based communication in multi-model inference.
candidates.reason: 言語エージェント間のテキスト通信のプリフィル遅延を避けるため、下流モデルへ上流モデルのKVキャッシュを学習なしで線形補間して融合するCacheFuseを提案しTTFTを最大12.2倍高速化する点を要旨が示しており、KVキャッシュ共有による多モデル推論への直接貢献として採用する。
